datasets.grain: one row per (TenantId, TraceId), latest version only

columns.name: TraceId
columns.description: Trace identifier, unique within the project.

columns.name: TraceName
columns.description: Display name of the trace, empty when none was recorded.

columns.name: OccurredAt

columns.name: UpdatedAt

columns.name: TotalDurationMs

columns.name: TimeToFirstTokenMs
columns.description: Milliseconds until the first generated token.

columns.description: Generation throughput over the trace.

columns.name: SpanCount
columns.description: Number of spans recorded under the trace.

columns.name: ContainsErrorStatus
columns.description: Whether any span of the trace ended in an error status.

columns.name: ContainsOKStatus
columns.description: Whether any span of the trace ended in an OK status.

columns.name: Models
columns.description: Every model used anywhere in the trace.

columns.name: TotalCost
columns.description: Billed cost of the trace, in USD.

columns.name: TokensEstimated

columns.name: TotalCompletionTokenCount
columns.description: Completion tokens across the trace.

columns.name: SatisfactionScore

columns.name: TopicId

columns.name: SubTopicId
columns.description: Sub-topic the trace was clustered into.

columns.name: ContainsPrompt
columns.description: Whether the trace used a managed prompt.

columns.name: SelectedPromptId
columns.description: Managed prompt selected for the trace.

columns.name: LastUsedPromptId
columns.description: Last managed prompt used in the trace.

columns.name: LastUsedPromptVersionId
columns.description: Version of the last managed prompt used.

columns.name: LastUsedPromptVersionNumber
columns.description: Version number of the last managed prompt used.

columns.name: SourceType
columns.description: Which product surface produced the trace.

columns.name: Attributes

columns.name: CapturedInput

columns.name: CapturedOutput

SELECT TraceId, TraceName, OccurredAt

traceFilter.syntax:
# Trace query syntax

A small Lucene-flavored language for filtering traces. Every clause is a
`field:value` pair joined by boolean operators. Free text without a field
matches against trace input/output.

## Quick start

| Goal | Query |
| --- | --- |
| Failing traces | `status:error` |
| Failing OpenAI traces | `status:error AND model:gpt-*` |
| Either failing or warning | `status:error OR status:warning` |
| Slow and expensive | `duration:>5000 AND cost:>0.10` |
| Mention of "refund" anywhere | `refund` |

## Grammar

```
query     = clause ( WS boolean WS clause )*
clause    = [NOT WS] (term | "(" query ")")
term      = field ":" value | freeText
boolean   = "AND" | "OR"
field     = identifier
value     = exact | wildcard | comparison | range | quoted
exact     = literal
wildcard  = literal containing "*"
comparison= (">" | ">=" | "<" | "<=") number
range     = "[" number "TO" number "]"
quoted    = "\"" anything "\""
freeText  = literal | quoted
```

- Operators (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`) are case-sensitive and **must be uppercase**.
- `NOT` and the shorthand `-` both negate the next clause.
- Parentheses group clauses: `(status:error OR status:warning) AND model:gpt-4o`.
- A bare token like `refund` searches free text — no field prefix required.

## Operators

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AND` | both must match | `status:error AND model:gpt-4o` |
| `OR` | either may match | `origin:simulation OR origin:evaluation` |
| `NOT` / `-` | negate next clause | `NOT status:ok` · `-status:ok` |
| `( … )` | grouping | `(status:error OR status:warning) AND service:web` |

## Value forms

| Form | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact match | `model:gpt-4o` | Case-insensitive for categorical fields. |
| Wildcard | `model:gpt-*` | `*` matches any characters. |
| Comparison | `cost:>0.05` · `duration:<=1000` | Numeric / range fields only. |
| Range | `cost:[0.01 TO 1.00]` | Inclusive on both ends. |
| Quoted | `user:"alice@example.com"` | Required if the value contains spaces or special characters. |
| Free text | `refund` · `"refund policy"` | Searches trace input/output. |

## Attributes

Three open-ended namespaces let you query arbitrary OTel attributes without
adding them to the static fields table. One per place an attribute can live:

| Form | Matches | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trace.attribute.<key>:value` | trace-level attribute equality (`Attributes[key]`) | `trace.attribute.langwatch.user_id:alice` |
| `span.attribute.<key>:value` | per-span attribute across every span in the trace (`SpanAttributes[key]`) | `span.attribute.gen_ai.request.model:gpt-5-mini` |
| `event.attribute.<key>:value` | per-event attribute across every span event in the trace | `event.attribute.exception.type:TimeoutError` |
| `event:<name>` | bare event-name filter (no dot in the field) | `event:tool_call` |
| `has:trace.attribute.<key>` | trace has *any* value at `Attributes[key]` | `has:trace.attribute.gen_ai.conversation.id` |
| `none:trace.attribute.<key>` | trace has no value at `Attributes[key]` | `none:trace.attribute.langwatch.user_id` |

Write the namespaced prefixes above. Two older spellings are still accepted so
saved views and older scripts keep working: `attribute.<key>` means
`trace.attribute.<key>`, and `event.<key>` means `event.attribute.<key>`.
There is no older spelling for the span namespace.

The dot is the disambiguator — `event:foo` matches an event *name*, and
`event.attribute.foo:bar` matches an event *attribute*.

## Limitations & gotchas

- Operators must be uppercase. `status:error and model:gpt-4o` is **invalid** — write `AND`.
- A trailing colon with no value (`status:`) is a syntax error. Provide a value or remove the clause.
- Mixing `OR` across different fields (`status:error OR model:gpt-4o`) works but bypasses the sidebar facets — prefer staying within one field per `OR` chain.
- Attribute matching is exact equality only — wildcards (`trace.attribute.foo:*ar`) and ranges (`trace.attribute.tokens:>10`) aren't yet supported on the dynamic namespaces.

endpoints.description: Search traces. Send the filter string as `filter`; it is combined with `query`, `filters` and `traceIds`.
What the fields hold. Without `field`, every facet with its top values; with `field`, that field's values and counts.
One trace in full, or as an LLM-readable digest with `format=digest`.

examples.title: The most recent traces that failed
examples.text:
SELECT TraceId, TraceName, OccurredAt, TotalDurationMs
FROM analytics.traces
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 1)
  AND ContainsErrorStatus
ORDER BY OccurredAt DESC
LIMIT 100

examples.title: Error rate per day over a month
examples.text:
SELECT
  toStartOfDay(OccurredAt) AS day,
  count() AS traces,
  countIf(ContainsErrorStatus) AS errors
FROM analytics.traces
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 30)
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day
examples.notes: A rate is two counts, not a division: keep the numerator and the denominator as columns so a zero-denominator bucket reads as zero traffic rather than as a null rate.

examples.title: Latency percentiles over a week
examples.text:
SELECT
  quantile(0.5)(TotalDurationMs) AS p50_ms,
  quantile(0.95)(TotalDurationMs) AS p95_ms,
  quantile(0.99)(TotalDurationMs) AS p99_ms
FROM analytics.traces
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 7)

examples.title: Traffic and errors per hour from the rollup
examples.text:
SELECT
  toStartOfHour(BucketStart) AS hour,
  sum(TraceCount) AS traces,
  sum(ErrorCount) AS errors
FROM analytics.trace_metrics_by_minute
WHERE BucketStart >= subtractDays(now(), 2)
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour
examples.notes: The per-minute rollup is already aggregated, so this reads far less than the same question over `traces`. Prefer it whenever the answer is a count or a sum over time.

examples.title: Spend and tokens by model over a week
examples.text:
SELECT
  Model,
  sum(CostSum) AS cost_usd,
  sum(PromptTokensSum + CompletionTokensSum) AS tokens
FROM analytics.model_usage_by_minute
WHERE BucketStart >= subtractDays(now(), 7)
GROUP BY Model
ORDER BY cost_usd DESC
LIMIT 50

examples.title: The longest conversations of the week
examples.text:
SELECT
  ConversationId,
  count() AS turns,
  min(OccurredAt) AS started_at,
  max(OccurredAt) AS last_turn
FROM analytics.trace_metrics
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 7)
  AND ConversationId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ConversationId
ORDER BY turns DESC
LIMIT 50
examples.notes: `trace_metrics` is the dataset that carries conversation, user and customer identity. There is no conversations dataset: a conversation is a group of traces sharing this id.

examples.title: Pass rate per evaluator
examples.text:
SELECT
  EvaluatorName,
  count() AS evaluations,
  countIf(Passed = 1) AS passed
FROM analytics.evaluations
WHERE ScheduledAt >= subtractDays(now(), 7)
  AND Status = 'processed'
GROUP BY EvaluatorName
ORDER BY evaluations DESC
LIMIT 50
examples.notes: Filter on a processed status: scheduled, skipped and errored rows carry no verdict and would dilute the rate.

examples.title: Which traces have the slowest single span
examples.text:
SELECT
  t.TraceId AS TraceId,
  t.TraceName AS TraceName,
  count() AS spans,
  max(s.DurationMs) AS slowest_span_ms
FROM analytics.traces AS t
INNER JOIN analytics.spans AS s
  ON s.TenantId = t.TenantId AND s.TraceId = t.TraceId
WHERE t.OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 1)
  AND s.StartTime >= subtractDays(now(), 1)
GROUP BY TraceId, TraceName
ORDER BY slowest_span_ms DESC
LIMIT 50
examples.notes: Bound the time column on BOTH sides of a join. The join key does not prune partitions, so a predicate on one side alone leaves the other side reading all of time.

examples.title: One user's traces, with the lookback as a parameter
examples.text:
SELECT
  TraceId,
  OccurredAt,
  Attributes['langwatch.user_id'] AS user_id
FROM analytics.traces
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), {days:UInt32})
  AND Attributes['langwatch.user_id'] = {user_id:String}
ORDER BY OccurredAt DESC
LIMIT 100

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The user id as it was sent on the trace.

examples.notes: Read one attribute key by name. Never select the whole `Attributes` map: it is the widest column on the dataset and almost none of it is the answer.

examples.title: Simulation runs that failed
examples.text:
SELECT ScenarioRunId, Name, Verdict, StartedAt
FROM analytics.simulations
WHERE StartedAt >= subtractDays(now(), 7)
  AND Verdict = 'failure'
ORDER BY StartedAt DESC
LIMIT 50

examples.title: Export captured input and output, page by page
examples.text:
SELECT OccurredAt AS after_ts, TraceId AS after_id, CapturedInput, CapturedOutput
FROM analytics.traces
WHERE OccurredAt >= subtractDays(now(), 7)
  AND (OccurredAt, TraceId) > ({after_ts:DateTime64(3)}, {after_id:String})
ORDER BY OccurredAt, TraceId
LIMIT 1000

parameters.name: after_ts
parameters.description: The previous page's last `OccurredAt`. Start from '1970-01-01 00:00:00.000'.

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description: The previous page's last `TraceId`. Start from the empty string.

examples.notes: The query API has no pagination of its own. This is the shape that pages without rewriting the statement, which is what `langwatch query --page-by keyset` rebinds between pages. The two ordering columns are aliased to the cursor parameters' own names, which is where the next page's cursor is read from: alias whichever columns you order by, or the walk cannot tell them from any other value in the row.

A tool call that failed
A phrase anywhere in the captured input or output

decisionTable.when: Find the traces matching a condition, and read them
decisionTable.why: It returns whole traces with their spans and evaluations. LangWatchQL returns columns, not traces.

decisionTable.when: Filter on an attribute you send yourself, or on an evaluator's verdict
decisionTable.use: Trace filter, with a `trace.attribute.` / `span.attribute.` / `event.attribute.` prefix or an evaluator field
decisionTable.why: The filter reaches attribute maps and span events by key. In LangWatchQL an attribute is a map lookup on one dataset and a span event is not exposed at all.

decisionTable.when: Free text anywhere in the captured input or output
decisionTable.use: Trace filter, as a bare term or a quoted phrase
decisionTable.why: The search is backed by a text index. The same question in SQL is a scan of the widest columns there are.

decisionTable.when: A count, a rate, a sum, a percentile, or any of them over time
decisionTable.why: One aggregate answers what would otherwise be a page-by-page walk of the whole result.

decisionTable.when: Group by model, evaluator, user, conversation or topic
decisionTable.why: `trace_metrics` and the per-minute rollups carry those identities already grouped. The filter has no GROUP BY.

decisionTable.when: Join traces to their spans or their evaluations
decisionTable.use: LangWatchQL, with the time column bounded on both sides
decisionTable.why: It is the only language with joins.

decisionTable.when: Export many rows for training or offline analysis
decisionTable.use: LangWatchQL with the keyset paging shape, or POST /api/traces/search with its scroll cursor
decisionTable.why: Both page without re-reading. Pick LangWatchQL when you want columns, the search when you want whole traces.

decisionTable.when: You do not know how a value is spelled
decisionTable.why: The reference lists the fields and their static vocabularies. Only the facets endpoint knows what this project actually holds.
